info.title: CF Meet Developer Platform internal API
info.description: HTTP surface of services/developer-platform: GET /health, GET /ready, the service-authenticated /internal/v1 API and (cfmeet.developer-platform.http-api) the gateway-forwarded customer API under /v1. Every /internal/v1 path, unknown ones included, requires a valid Ed25519 service token whose issuer the Developer Platform's trust bundle grants the route's permission. Customers never reach this service directly: the API Gateway authenticates them (Platform Access credentials, or the CF Meet session verified through the Meeting Service bridge) and forwards a signed request. Section 53: POST /internal/v1/platform/events (developer-event.publish) ingests committed producer events for central customer webhooks, and the gateway-forwarded machine webhook API is served at Calling's public paths (/v1/webhooks*, /v1/webhook-deliveries/{delivery_id}/replay) for the cut-over. 1.5.0 Section 53 §9.1 / §19.3 webhook migration operator routes under /internal/v1/operator/webhook-migration/** (status, dry-run inventory, resumable import, reconcile, shadow report, cutover check, rotation acknowledgements, takeover, rollback export, rollback). 1.6.0 (Part VI Chapters 10–13): usage fact ingestion, stream watermarks and reconciliation (developer-event.publish), entitlement snapshots with caller restrictions, operator production-access decisions, overrides, first-party scope grants, usage operations, cost-centre usage, support profiles and the forwarded /v1/usage and /v1/limits. 1.7.0 (Chapters 14–18): conflicting event replays refused (CONFLICTING_REPLAY) and GET /internal/v1/operator/ingestion/health. 1.8.0 (Part VI §19.4): forwardedListUsage / forwardedGetLimits answer the PUBLISHED Calling contract of GET /v1/usage and GET /v1/limits (platform/usage UsageList / Limits, Calling's parameters and VALIDATION_ERROR rules): Calling's metered call facts projected from the unified ledger and the gateway-enforced REQUEST_RATE; Calling-only detail stays at GET /v1/calling/usage and GET /v1/calling/limits. 1.9.0 (Blueprint Section 15, PLT-009): operator-only reads GET /internal/v1/operator/organizations (list / search) and GET /internal/v1/operator/activity (organization-scoped and platform-level operator commands); platform-level operator commands are now audited.

post.description: Section 53: a producer (Meeting Service, Calling, Privacy Relay, Messaging, Numbering, SMS Gateway) publishes a committed domain event from its transactional outbox (platform envelope). Permission `developer-event.publish`; the envelope's producer_service must be the authenticated caller and its runtime_environment the receiver's; its type must belong to the producer's own domain (unknown families are refused). The event is projected into the public catalog (allow-listed safe keys only; never stored or forwarded verbatim), deduplicated on (producer, event_id) — a duplicate returns the same eventId and creates no delivery — and fanned out to the ACTIVE matching subscriptions of the SAME application environment (recorded SHADOW in shadow mode). 200 = accepted (also for internal-only facts, eventId null); 400 = refused (do not retry); 503 = retry later. Behind DEVELOPER_PLATFORM_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED (off: 404). A publication that conflicts with the native event already recorded under the same (producer, event_id) — another type, ownership scope, time or projected payload — is refused 400 `CONFLICTING_REPLAY` and recorded for operators; the original event is kept.

Requires webhooks.manage. Every subscribed event type also requires its own read scope (call.* calls.read, voicemail.* enterprise.voicemail.read, recording.* / artifact.* enterprise.recording.read, relay.* privacy.sessions.read, usage.* / limit.* usage.read, sms.* sms.read, conversation.* / message.* messages.read, number.* numbers.read, credential.* credentials.manage, production_access.* production_access.request; meeting.* / participant.* need webhooks.manage only). The endpoint must be a public https URL (re-checked at delivery and connection time; redirects never followed). The signing secret is returned ONCE. Machine credentials only (the console uses /v1/environments/{environmentId}/webhooks); scope (tenant, application, environment) is the credential's confirmed chain: another environment's subscription is 404. Gateway-forwarded: the API Gateway's service token (developer-request.forward) with the signed delegated context naming the authenticated credential; the public contract of this path is Calling's (cfmeet.calling.http-api, cfmeet.platform.webhooks) and the gateway re-points it here when API_GATEWAY_CENTRAL_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED. Behind DEVELOPER_PLATFORM_GATEWAY_API_ENABLED and DEVELOPER_PLATFORM_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED (off: 404).

post.description: Section 53 §9.1 / §19.3 webhook migration from Calling (operator tooling). Permission `developer-platform.administer` (operator console only) and a named human operator. Imports Calling's subscriptions, events, deliveries and attempts with their ids. Resumes the open run from its checkpoint (each page and its checkpoint commit together), else starts a full run; idempotent (upserts keyed by Calling's ids; a subscription is updated only when Calling's version is newer and it is unchanged here; a delivery still open at Calling is a held mirror). Signing secrets arrive only transfer-sealed and are re-sealed under this deployment's key ring; a secret that cannot be carried over makes the subscription ROTATION_REQUIRED (DISABLED, no secret) — never substituted. 503 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE without the transfer key, the key ring or CF_CALLING_BASE_URL. Audited.

post.summary: Take over webhook delivery from Calling
post.description: Section 53 §9.1 / §19.3 webhook migration from Calling (operator tooling). Permission `developer-platform.administer` (operator console only) and a named human operator. The delivery switch. Refused (409 INVALID_STATE) unless this platform delivers (DEVELOPER_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_MODE=active), Calling stopped sending (CALLING_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_ENABLED=false, no live claim) and the last completed import started after that. Releases the held mirrors of Calling's open deliveries (same delivery and event ids, attempts continued), de-duplicates every logical delivery to exactly one sender and moves to CUT_OVER (deliveries to migrated subscriptions are sent only from then on). Audited.

post.summary: Roll webhook delivery back to Calling
post.description: Section 53 §9.1 / §19.3 webhook migration from Calling (operator tooling). Permission `developer-platform.administer` (operator console only) and a named human operator. Rolls the delivery switch back: refused unless the phase is CUT_OVER / ROLLED_BACK and Calling's delivery is still disabled; moves to ROLLED_BACK (nothing is sent here any more; refused while a claim here is live), settles at Calling every open delivery already delivered here and hands every other open delivery back to Calling. Deliveries of events Calling never recorded are reported as orphans (the rollback stops unless acceptOrphans). Audited.

get.description: Section 55 / §19.4 ownership migration: Calling's public `GET /v1/limits` path served by the Developer Platform once the API Gateway re-points it. Keeps the published contract (`getLimits`): REQUEST_RATE (MINUTE) of the credential's effective plan entitlement (the limit the gateway enforces; current = API operations the ledger recorded this minute). Concurrent calls, telecom spend and the PRINCIPAL axis (`principalId`, refused here with VALIDATION_ERROR) are Calling's: `GET /v1/calling/limits`. `usage.read`. Permission `developer-request.forward`.

parameters.name: principalId
parameters.description: Refused (400 VALIDATION_ERROR): the PRINCIPAL axis is served by Calling at GET /v1/calling/limits.

get.description: Part VI §17: ingestion health. `DEGRADED` while a usage fact or platform event was refused in the last 24 hours or a shadow reconciliation mismatched in the last 7 days; counts per producer (no payloads) and the producers' export watermarks. Permission `developer-platform.administer`.

serviceToken.name: X-CF-Service-Authorization
serviceToken.description: Ed25519 compact JWS (typ cf-service+jwt) from packages/service-auth, audience cfmeet.developer-platform.

platform-developer.common.v1.Error.description: Error envelope (Cache-Control: no-store). Messages never contain an identifier, credential, token or database text.

platform-developer.common.v1.GatewayCont.description: GET /internal/v1/gateway/context: the canonical Platform Access ids of the caller's application environment, as Platform Access re-validated them from the API Gateway's signed delegated context.

platform-developer.control.v1.ActivityEv.description: Safe change summary: opaque ids, codes and display metadata only — never secrets, credentials, contacts or E2EE material.

platform-developer.control.v1.BillingAcc.description: Billing-account REFERENCE metadata. Never card, bank, charge or balance data.

platform-developer.control.v1.Commercial.description: An immutable commercial plan version. No price exists in Part VI.

subject.description: Internal reads with serviceAccountId / credentialId: the caller's own (never higher) limits and levels; the top-level values stay the environment's.

platform-developer.control.v1.Entitlemen.description: Effective platform entitlements (Section 54 §10.4 precedence: organization plan, explicit operator override, stricter project plan, environment cap, service-account and credential restrictions; the most restrictive value wins and the limiting level is named). Internal reads also carry the versioned snapshot consuming services cache.

token.description: One-time acceptance token, returned ONLY in this response (stored as a digest; never readable again).

platform-developer.control.v1.OperatorAc.description: Section 15 (PLT-009): one operator command — an OPERATOR event of an organization's activity (scope ORGANIZATION) or a platform-level command such as a plan publication or a usage rebuild (scope PLATFORM, organizationId null).

platform-developer.control.v1.OperatorOr.description: Section 15 (PLT-009): an organization as listed to operators (no member role; who created it and whether a rename still has to reach Platform Access).

id.description: The organization id IS the canonical Platform Access tenant id.

classification.description: Platform Access tenant classification (operator-controlled; GET of one organization only).

platform-developer.control.v1.Organizati.description: The organization id IS the canonical Platform Access tenant id.

platform-developer.control.v1.Production.description: Section 55 production-access request: SANDBOX_READY → PRODUCTION_REQUESTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED / REJECTED → LIVE / SUSPENDED.

platform-developer.control.v1.Role.description: Part VI workspace role (Section 50 permission matrix).

platform-developer.control.v1.SupportPro.description: Section 57 support / incident routing metadata: member references only, no ticket content, emails or phone numbers.

platform-developer.control.v1.UsageFactS.description: A producer's usage fact (cf_usage_facts wire format); the digest is the canonical payload digest.

url.description: Public https endpoint. Server-side validation additionally refuses every loopback / private / link-local / CGNAT / metadata address and re-checks the resolved address at connection time (DNS rebinding); redirects are never followed.

platform-developer.webhooks.v1.DeliveryS.description: FAILED is the dead letter (replayable). SHADOW: recorded while the platform ran in shadow mode before the cut-over; deliberately not sent.

platform-developer.webhooks.v1.PublishEv.description: POST /internal/v1/platform/events: accepted. A duplicate (same producer and source event id) returns the same event id; an internal-only fact of the producer's domain has none.

url.description: Public https endpoint. Server-side validation additionally refuses every loopback / private / link-local / CGNAT / metadata address and re-checks the resolved address at connection time (DNS rebinding); redirects are never followed.

platform-developer.webhooks.v1.Webhook.description: The customer view of a subscription (Calling's contract; never the signing secret).

platform-developer.webhooks.v1.WebhookEv.description: The public event catalog: Calling, Privacy Relay, SMS Gateway and Messaging families (Part G §68, unchanged) plus the Section 53 meeting, participant, artifact, number, credential and production-access families.

signingSecret.description: Returned ONLY by create and rotate-secret; never readable again.

platform.common.v1.ApplicationEnvironmen.description: Kind of a customer application environment (Part B section 7).

platform.common.v1.CorrelationId.description: Server-generated identifier that stays stable across every hop of one causal operation.

platform.common.v1.RequestId.description: Server-generated identifier of one request / one service hop.

platform.common.v1.RuntimeEnvironment.description: Deployment/runtime environment of a service identity. Not the same dimension as a customer's application environment (SANDBOX / TEST / PRODUCTION).

platform.common.v1.ServiceId.description: Stable, product-independent identity of a deployable CF Meet backend service, e.g. cfmeet.calling, cfmeet.privacy-relay, cfmeet.telephony, cfmeet.platform-access, cfmeet.numbering, cfmeet.sms-gateway, cfmeet.messaging, cfmeet.developer-platform, cfmeet.api-gateway. Never a wildcard.

platform.events.envelope.v1.title: CF Meet cross-service durable event envelope v1
platform.events.envelope.v1.description: Infrastructure envelope for durable cross-service events. Producers persist events transactionally (outbox) with the state change they describe. The payload is described by its own registered contract identified by event_type and schema_version (Calling: cfmeet.calling.call-lifecycle-event for every calling.* event type). The envelope never carries secrets, service tokens, customer credentials, provider credentials, telephone numbers or protected contact plaintext.

event_type.description: Dot-separated event type, prefixed by the producing domain.

schema_version.description: Major version of the payload contract.

causation_id.description: event_id of the event that caused this one, if any.

ownership.description: Owning customer scope of the event subject, when the subject belongs to a tenant.

payload.description: Event payload (validated against its own contract). Top-level keys are snake_case; keys that name secrets or contact data are refused.

scope.description: The level: the API-client chain TENANT → APPLICATION → SERVICE_ACCOUNT → CREDENTIAL (every configured parent is also an aggregate ceiling), the independent PRINCIPAL axis (only for a principal resolved in the caller's scope, `?principalId=`), the ENVIRONMENT telecom-spend policy. Never an identifier.

platform.usage.v1.LimitStatus.description: One limit: every configured level — the API-client chain TENANT → APPLICATION → SERVICE_ACCOUNT → CREDENTIAL, the requested principal's PRINCIPAL axis, and the environment's telecom-spend policy for spend — with ceiling / current / remaining, and the BINDING level (least remaining) at the top level. No level carries an identifier.

platform.usage.v1.ResourceClass.description: APP_MEDIA: application call / participant / session connected time. PUBLIC_NETWORK: one public telephone-network leg. STORAGE: a stored voicemail message or call recording.

platform.usage.v1.UsageCost.description: Cost EVIDENCE of a public-network leg, not a price or a charge. KNOWN: reported by the network provider. ESTIMATED: an estimate the provider did not confirm. UNKNOWN: no figure exists — it carries no amount (never zero).

platform.usage.v1.UsageRecord.description: One FINAL consumption fact (Part G §69). Recorded once per subject (idempotent): a late or repeated provider event never changes or doubles it.

quantity.description: Connected time, or the stored artifact's duration.

destinationCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the public destination — never the number.
